mainTopicBrief: 本单元围绕生命科学与健康展开，涵盖基因编辑的前景与伦理（Reading）、针灸与传统医学（Extended reading）和守护视力健康（Integrated skills）三个子话题——健康与科技伦理既是高考应用文'倡议/介绍'类的常客，也是雅思科技与健康类议论文的核心命题。

subTopics.title: 基因编辑：机遇与伦理
subTopics.desc: 课文核心：none are as game-changing as genome editing——它是 an effective means of disease treatment and prevention，但 as the technology develops at a fast pace, questions arise about how to use it appropriately。

prompts.task: 上周你参加了学校举办的基因科学讲座。请你用英文为校刊写一篇短文，内容包括：1. 讲座的主要内容；2. 你印象最深的部分；3. 你的感想。注意：词数100左右。
prompts.reference:
Last Friday, our school invited a professor from a local university to give a lecture on genome editing, and I was lucky enough to attend.

The professor explained that genes play a critical role in shaping our lives, and that genome editing is considered an effective means of disease treatment and prevention. By correcting abnormal genes early on, doctors may even make it possible to prevent some diseases from ever developing. No wonder many scientists see it as a new weapon in the fight against diseases.

What impressed me most, however, was the discussion at the end. As the technology continues to develop at a fast pace, questions arise about how to use it appropriately. Science, I realised, needs both courage and caution.
vocabHints: play a critical role in shaping our lives
an effective means of disease treatment and prevention
make it possible to prevent diseases from developing
a new weapon in the fight against diseases

prompts.task: Genetic research is developing rapidly. Some people believe it brings great benefits to humanity, while others worry that it interferes with nature and may be misused. Discuss both views and give your own opinion. (Write at least 250 words.)
prompts.reference:
Few scientific advances provoke stronger feelings than genetic research. Enthusiasts foresee the conquest of hereditary disease, while critics warn of arrogance toward nature and the abuse of power. After considering both positions, I believe the research should continue, but only inside firm ethical walls.

The promise is difficult to overstate. Thousands of disorders arise from faulty genes, and therapies that repair these errors could spare families generations of suffering. Genetic screening already helps doctors match treatments to individual patients, and modified crops resist drought in regions where harvest failure once meant famine. To halt such work would be to choose, knowingly, the continuation of preventable misery.

The dangers, however, are equally real. Techniques able to cure can also be used to enhance, and a market in "designer" advantages would harden social inequality into biology itself. Errors introduced into human embryos would pass to future generations who never consented, and genetic data held by insurers or governments invites discrimination. History shows that when powerful technologies outrun regulation, the poor and voiceless pay first.

The sensible course is therefore neither prohibition nor a free market, but strict governance: international rules that distinguish therapy from enhancement, independent review of experiments, transparency about results, and severe penalties for misuse. Nuclear technology, similarly double-edged, has been managed this way for decades — imperfectly, yet without catastrophe.

In conclusion, genetic research is a race between wisdom and recklessness. Its medical rewards are too great to abandon, but they will remain blessings only if law and ethics advance at the same pace as the science itself.

subTopics.title: 别把自己封闭起来
subTopics.desc: 语法板块核心词块：withdraw into oneself、equip oneself with、hold on——身心健康不仅是身体的事，也在于不把自己封闭起来，学会向外求助、坚持下去。

prompts.task: 你的好友最近考试失利，变得沉默孤僻，不愿与人来往。请你用英文给他写一封信，内容包括：1. 表达理解；2. 给出建议；3. 表达支持。注意：词数100左右。
prompts.reference:
Dear Chris,

I've noticed that since the exam you've grown quiet and seem to have withdrawn into yourself. I understand — disappointment is heavy, and everyone needs time. But please don't shut yourself away for too long.

One bad result does not decide who you are. Try to equip yourself with a small plan: talk to a teacher about what went wrong, break the next goal into tiny steps, and let a friend walk part of the way with you. When it feels hard, just hold on — feelings, like weather, always change.

I'm here whenever you want to talk, or simply to sit in silence together. You are not alone in this.

Yours,
Li Hua
vocabHints: does not decide who you are
equip yourself with a small plan
break the goal into tiny steps

prompts.task: In many countries, mental health problems among young people are becoming more common. What are the causes of this problem, and what measures could be taken to address it? (Write at least 250 words.)
prompts.reference:
Across many countries, anxiety and depression among young people are rising sharply. Understanding why, and deciding how to respond, has become an urgent task for schools and societies alike.

Several causes stand out. Academic pressure is intense: students face relentless competition for grades and university places, and many judge their whole worth by results. Social media adds a second burden, exposing the young to a constant stream of edited, idealised lives against which their own feel inadequate, while replacing face-to-face friendship with shallower online contact. A third factor is isolation — as families grow busier and communities looser, troubled teenagers often withdraw into themselves rather than reach out for help, partly because mental illness still carries a stigma that keeps suffering hidden.

Fortunately, the problem can be eased. Schools should treat mental health as seriously as physical health, teaching pupils to recognise warning signs and providing counsellors they can approach without shame. Reducing the obsessive focus on examinations, and helping students value effort and wellbeing over ranking, would remove a major source of stress. Families and society, meanwhile, must equip young people with the confidence to talk openly, so that a struggling teenager holds on and seeks support instead of shutting the world out. Sensible limits on social-media use would help too.

In conclusion, the growing mental-health crisis among the young springs mainly from academic pressure, social media and isolation. With open conversation, accessible support and a healthier definition of success, much of this suffering can be prevented — and no investment repays a society more richly than the wellbeing of its young.

subTopics.title: 守护视力健康
subTopics.desc: 综合技能板块核心：近视数据 fuel concerns about eyesight problems——The figures disturb the school authorities, who have decided to tackle this problem head-on。

prompts.task: 针对学生近视率上升的问题，请你以学生会名义用英文写一份倡议书，内容包括：1. 说明现状；2. 提出两三条护眼建议；3. 发出号召。注意：词数100左右。
prompts.reference:
Dear fellow students,

Recent figures about the number of short-sighted students in our school have fuelled concerns about eyesight problems, and the school authorities have decided to tackle this problem head-on. As members of the Student Union, we hereby propose the following.

First, give your eyes a break. After every forty minutes of study, look into the distance or do eye exercises. Second, limit screen time — try not to bury yourself in your phone before bedtime. Third, spend more time outdoors, as natural light protects our eyes.

Bright eyes light up a bright future. Let's take action now, before thick glasses become part of everyone's face!

The Student Union

prompts.task: The health of young people is declining partly because they spend too much time on electronic devices. Some people think schools should be responsible for solving this problem, while others believe parents should. Discuss both views and give your own opinion. (Write at least 250 words.)
prompts.reference:
As screens absorb ever more of childhood, doctors report rising short-sightedness, poorer sleep and weaker fitness among the young. Society agrees the problem is urgent but argues about whose duty it is to act: the school's or the family's. My position is that parents bear the primary responsibility, while schools serve as indispensable partners.

Those who look to schools have logic on their side. Children spend the better part of their waking hours in class, and teachers command both expertise and authority. Schools can schedule daily exercise, teach the science of eye care and healthy habits, restrict phone use on campus, and spot problems early through routine health checks. Because they reach every child, school policies also protect those whose parents lack the time or knowledge to help.

Nevertheless, the decisive battleground is the home. It is parents who buy the devices, set — or fail to set — limits on evening use, choose between outdoor weekends and indoor ones, and model behaviour itself: a father scrolling through dinner teaches more powerfully than any poster in a corridor. Habits formed at home also operate during holidays and weekends, precisely when screen time peaks. Where families enforce reasonable rules, school campaigns take root; where they do not, even the strictest timetable is undone at the front gate.

In conclusion, responsibility is shared but not equal. Schools should educate, organise activity and restrain use within their walls, yet the daily decisions that shape a child's health are made at home. The most effective arrangement is an alliance in which teachers supply knowledge and structure, while parents supply consistent enforcement and a living example.

subTopics.title: 针灸与传统医学
subTopics.desc: 拓展阅读核心：There is evidence that acupuncture dates back to the Stone Age, when stone tools called bian were used to press areas of the body——针灸是中医智慧的活化石。

prompts.task: 你校下周六将举办中医文化体验日活动。请你用英文给对中国文化感兴趣的外国朋友 Leo 写一封邮件，邀请他参加，内容包括：1. 活动时间地点；2. 活动内容（如针灸展示）；3. 表达期待。注意：词数100左右。
prompts.reference:
Dear Leo,

How is everything going? Knowing that you have been interested in traditional Chinese culture, I'm writing to invite you to a Traditional Chinese Medicine experience day at our school hall next Saturday, starting at 9 a.m.

The highlight will be acupuncture. There is evidence that acupuncture dates back to the Stone Age, when stone tools were used to press areas of the body. Today doctors use fine needles instead, and many patients find it helpful for pain relief. During the activity, a doctor from a local TCM hospital will demonstrate how it works, and we can also learn to recognise common Chinese herbs.

I'm sure the day will offer you a window into Chinese wisdom. Looking forward to your reply.

Yours,
Li Hua
vocabHints: date back to the Stone Age

prompts.task: Traditional medicine is becoming more popular in many countries. Some people trust traditional treatments more than modern medicine, while others doubt their effectiveness. Discuss both views and give your own opinion. (Write at least 250 words.)
prompts.reference:
In many countries, clinics offering herbal remedies, acupuncture and other time-honoured treatments now stand beside modern hospitals, and patients increasingly wonder which door to enter. Some trust tradition; others trust only laboratory science. In my view the two approaches are complements rather than rivals, though scientific testing must remain the final judge.

Supporters of traditional medicine offer respectable arguments. Therapies refined over many centuries embody accumulated observation of the human body, and several — acupuncture for pain relief being the best-known example — have earned recognition from mainstream researchers. Traditional practice also tends to treat the patient as a whole person, addressing sleep, diet and stress where a rushed prescription may not, and it is often cheaper and more culturally familiar, which matters greatly in communities where hospitals feel foreign.

Sceptics reply that longevity is not proof. Remedies that were never properly tested may be useless or even harmful, and the gravest danger arises when patients abandon proven treatment for serious illness in favour of unverified alternatives. Cancer delayed is cancer advanced; no cultural respect can excuse that cost. Furthermore, an unregulated market invites fraud, with miracle cures sold to the desperate at their most vulnerable moment.

The reasonable settlement, I believe, is integration under evidence. Traditional therapies should be researched with the same rigour as new drugs: those that pass become part of medicine proper, as several already have, while those that fail should be honestly retired. Patients deserve both the accumulated wisdom of the past and the tested certainty of the present — a mature health system refuses to make them choose blindly between the two.
